newsitem.title: UK: EU wheat tender award big, but still disappoints.
newsitem.headline: EU wheat tender award big, but still disappoints.

text.p: The EU award of 477,700 tonnes of open-market wheat for export was the biggest so far this season, but it still dissappointed an excited trade.
Europe's grain market was roused out of a pre-holiday lull by the active bidding ahead of the tender and the result dampened spirits, traders said.
The grains management committee, which adjudicates the tender, could and should have done more, some felt.

The grains management committee in Brussels awarded licences for the export of 477,700 tonnes of open market wheat at a refund of 17.47 Ecus per tonne, which values French wheat for Jan at $152.45 per tonne fob, Reuters calculates.

Along with the 550,000 tonnes to be exported to Africa under contracts presented by traders wanting to take advantage of a special refund scheme, this means the EU arranged for the export of more than a million tonnes of wheat on Thursday.

The wheat awarded under the open market tenders is destined for a wide range of destinations, traders said. "It's going in all directions," one said. Possible destinations include North Africa, Iraq, and Eastern Europe and Russia. Russia, however, does not have the funds for new imports, traders said.
Talk in US grain markets has it that India has bought one million tonnes of Australian wheat, but U.S. exporters were awaiting confirmation of the deal, they said.
Indian food minister Devendra Prasad Yadav said on Thursday that India would import two million tonnes of wheat during fiscal 1996/97 (April-March).

The likely destination of the 76,550 tonnes of open market barley for which the EU granted licences is Saudi Arabia. The EU award prices the barley at around $134 per tonne basis French and rather less basis UK, traders said. "They've maintained exactly the same level as before," one said.

Exporters are still fulfilling sales already done to Saudi. And the country is in the market to import a further 500,000 tonnes of optional barley for February delivery onwards , European grain traders said.
Traders said Saudi Arabia had not yet officially announced a date for the tender.
European exporters currently had a supply advantage over the U.S. and Canada, where barley supplies are tight.
